text.p: Merrill Lynch has upgraded its profit forecast for MOL Rt and its opinion to "accumulate" from "neutral".

"From an operational standpoint, the outlook for the rest of 1996 is set to be boosted by continued high oil prices, in addition to lower financial charges and tax rate," analysts Tom Chadwick and Sue Graham said in a note to investors.
"We are thus raising our (1996) earnings per share (EPS) forecast from 98 forints to 134 forints to take account of this."
MOL, the largest stock on the Budapest Stock Exhange (BSE), has underperformed the market during most of this year.
Merrill Lynch left its EPS forecast unchanged at 278 forints for 1997 because it expected oil prices to decline after their recent rally but noted this will be offset by rises in gas prices.
"The extent remains unclear but we are assuming an 18 percent increase from prevailing levels," the analysts said. "Any improvement on this should be regarded positively."
Merrill Lynch has upgraded its forecast following the release of MOL's January-September results last week.
On the BSE, MOL shares stood at 1,630 forints, down 25, at 1212 GMT.
